- `app/Sources/ExportSheetController.swift` (523 lines) — in `loadView`, ids `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,cancel}` on `formatPopup`, `sizePopup`, `ratePopup`, `qualityPopup`, `loudnessPopup`, `rangePopup`, `exportButton`, `queueButton`, the local `cancelButton`.
- `app/Sources/InspectorSection.swift` — init sets its accessibility id `TutorialTargets.sectionPrefix + id`.
- `app/Sources/InspectorTabBadge.swift` — `tabRect(index:stripWidth:stripHeight:)`; the existing `tabRect(stripWidth:stripHeight:)` calls it with the Assistant's index.
- `app/Sources/UISnapshot.swift` — `WindowKind.tutorial`; `openWindow` and `kind(of:)` arms; the ring staged and unstaged with the fill; `rect(_ r: NSRect, in root: NSView)`.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+Snapshot.swift` — `.tutorial` with settings/welcome/recorder in `snapshotSubject`; the `window` description names it; staging gets the ring.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+Tutorials.swift` — `tutorial_state {target?}`, every answer's `panel` and `ring`, `tutorial_press`, the Show Me wait shared by `tutorial_step` and `tutorial_press`.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+DevTools.swift` — `tutorial_press` handler row, in `devOffMainTools`, its catalog row after `tutorialExitTool()`, docs.
- `app/Sources/UIMenuTable.swift` — `"startTutorial:": .window`, right before `openPracticeProject:`.
- `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json` — `startTutorial:` row before `openPracticeProject:` (verdict `window`, code ``app/Sources/AppDelegate+Tutorials.swift `func startTutorial(` ``, note: the coach panel, never an alert).
- `tools/proof/v2_menu.py` — writes `Tutorials.json` (`tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py --guide docs/guide --out <PROBE_DIR>/Tutorials.json`) beside its probe, as it copies the templates, so H1 sees the live per-page leaves.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift` — answer gains `unresolvable`; `tools/proof/tutorial_fixtures/facts.json` gains `"unresolvable": []`.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` — a problem when `unresolvable` is not an empty list; selftest case `target-unresolvable`; docstring counts.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_chrome_proof.py` (new) — the MCP proof (Approach 9).
- `tools/proof/dev_tools.py` — append `tutorial_press`; docstring. `tools/proof/assistant_session_proof.py:391` — `== 12` → `== 13`.
- `tools/proof/README.md` — "The tutorial chrome" section after "The tutorial runner"; the tutorials-checked counts.
- `docs/guide/tutorials.md` (new) — running a tutorial, the panel and its buttons, Show Me, the ring, the practice offer. `docs/guide/README.md` — its entry as 18, Menus becomes 19.
- `docs/guide/menus-and-shortcuts.md` — Help rows `Tutorials ▸ <page> ▸ <tutorial>`. `README.md` — a **Tutorials.** highlight linking the page. `docs/developing.md` — the dev-tool list names `tutorial_press`. `CONTEXT.md` — **Coach panel** and **Spotlight**.
- `docs/manual-checks.md` — TUT-3..TUT-6 (Approach 10).
- `designs/tutorials.md` — the TU3 record (numbers only as printed); TU4 left owed.

`tools/proof/graphics_menu_probe.swift` is NOT changed: Help's top-level titles stay `Frame Job Help, Tutorials, Graphics Reference`, and its probe has no `Tutorials.json`, so its Tutorials submenu is Open Practice Project alone. `tutorial_proof.py` is not changed.

## Interfaces
```swift
extension Notification.Name { static let tutorialRunnerDidChange: Notification.Name }  // object: the runner; posted on main
final class TutorialRunner { private(set) var revealRefused: String?   // was private (class body)
    var lastCompleted: (step: Int, by: TutorialAdvance)? { get } }   // completed.last
enum TutorialSentence { static func attributed(_ text: String, font: NSFont, boldFont: NSFont, codeFont: NSFont, color: NSColor) -> NSAttributedString
    static func plain(_ text: String) -> String }   // `**x**` → x, `` `x` `` → x; an unpaired marker stays literal
enum TutorialTargetKind: Equatable { case view(String), inspectorTab(InspectorTab), subTab(ClipSubTab), section(String), clip(TutorialClipSet) }
struct TutorialTargetSpot { let window: NSWindow?; let rect: NSRect?; let reason: String? }  // rect: window.contentView coords, clipped to what shows
enum TutorialTargetResolver {
    static func kind(of name: String) -> TutorialTargetKind?          // nil outside TutorialTargets
    static func resolve(_ name: String, in editor: EditorViewController, created: [UInt32]) -> TutorialTargetSpot
    static func bringIntoView(_ name: String, in editor: EditorViewController, created: [UInt32]) }
final class TutorialRingView: NSView { static let identifier = "tutorial.spotlight"; static let outset: CGFloat = 4; static let lineWidth: CGFloat = 2 }
final class TutorialSpotlightWindow: NSWindow {}
final class TutorialSpotlight { private(set) var target: String?; private(set) var spot: TutorialTargetSpot?
    func show(_ target: String?, in editor: EditorViewController, created: [UInt32], stepChanged: Bool); func hide(); func refreshSoon()
    func ringFrame(in window: NSWindow) -> NSRect? }                  // the ring view's frame in window.contentView coords, when shown there
enum TutorialPanelButton: String, CaseIterable { case back, showMe = "show_me", skip, next, exit, openPractice = "open_practice", close }
final class TutorialPanel: NSPanel {}                                  // canBecomeKey false, canBecomeMain false
final class TutorialPanelController: NSWindowController { static let tickHold: TimeInterval   // 0.8
    var onPress: ((TutorialPanelButton) -> Void)?
    func showStep(_ runner: TutorialRunner); func showOffer(title: String, sentence: String, message: String?)
    func state() -> [String: Any]; func button(_ b: TutorialPanelButton) -> NSButton? }   // shown and enabled, else nil
final class TutorialCoach { static let shared: TutorialCoach; private(set) weak var editor: EditorViewController?
    private(set) var panel: TutorialPanelController?; let spotlight: TutorialSpotlight
    func observe(); func start(id: String); func press(_ b: TutorialPanelButton)
    static func displayTitle(_ title: String) -> String               // first character uppercased, the rest as written
    static func frontEditor() -> EditorViewController?                // NSApp.mainWindow's editor, else the first editor in NSApp.orderedWindows
    static func panelOrigin(editor: NSRect, panel: NSSize, screen: NSRect) -> NSPoint
    static let noWindowSentence = "This tutorial runs in a project window."
    static let offerLine = "Open the practice project, or open a movie of your own (File ▸ Open…)." }
extension AppDelegate { @objc func startTutorial(_ sender: Any?) }   // (sender as? NSMenuItem)?.representedObject as? String
extension InspectorTabBadge { static func tabRect(index: Int, stripWidth: CGFloat, stripHeight: CGFloat) -> NSRect }
```
Dev tools (`snapshot_ui`'s `window` enum gains `tutorial`, refused with `project` or `view`). `panel` = `TutorialPanelController.state()` or null: `{shown, mode: "step"|"finished"|"offer", tutorial (id|null), title, progress, text (plain, as shown), message (string|null), buttons ([ids shown, in order]), enabled ([ids enabled]), tick (bool), project (served editor's path|null)}`. `ring` = `{target (name|null), shown, window ("editor"|"sheet"|null), rect ([x, top, w, h] in that window's content view, top-left origin, 2 dp; the visible TARGET rect, not outset)|null, reason (string|null)}`. `tutorial_state {target?}`: the TU2 answer plus `panel`, `ring` (the live spotlight, served editor only, else null) and, with `target`, `target: {name, shown, window, rect, reason}` resolved now (unknown name refused naming it). `tutorial_press {button: back|show_me|skip|next|exit|open_practice|close}` (off main; `project` refused — the panel belongs to no project): `performClick(nil)` on that panel button; refused "The tutorial panel is not up." / "The tutorial panel shows no <title> button now."; `show_me` waits as `tutorial_step` does; answers `{ok, panel, ring}` plus the served editor's TU2 state when one runs.

## Approach
1. **Spec §11 first** (TU-10, TU-11 as Approach 1–7), then the ids (pure tagging, no behaviour), then resolver, spotlight, panel, coach, menu, dev tools, proof, docs.
2. **The door (TU-10).** `tutorialsMenu()`: for each `TutorialLibrary.bundled()` page holding a decoded tutorial, in its order, a submenu titled the page's `title` holding `displayTitle(tutorial.title)` items (`startTutorial:`, `representedObject` the id, no key equivalent); then a separator; then Open Practice Project. A throwing or empty library gives Open Practice Project alone. No validator arm (enabled). `startTutorial` → `TutorialCoach.shared.start(id:)`. No `presentError`, `runModal` or sheet anywhere in TU3 (the inventory's grep sees no new site); every failure is panel text.
3. **The coach (TU-10).** `start(id:)`: an unknown/refused id → offer with the model's sentence; `frontEditor()` nil → offer `noWindowSentence` centred on `NSScreen.main`; else `TutorialRunner.start`; a `TutorialRefusal` → offer with its sentence beside that editor. The offer: title `displayTitle`, `sentence`, `message` = `offerLine`, buttons Open Practice Project, Close. **Open Practice Project**: `PracticeProject.open()`, its editor (`windowControllers…contentViewController as? EditorViewController`), then `TutorialRunner.start` there; a throw shows its `localizedDescription` as the message. **One tutorial at a time:** on `.tutorialRunnerDidChange` whose runner's editor is not the served one, the coach exits the served editor's runner and serves the new one (a dev-tool start included). Served: the panel shows the step beside the editor and the spotlight its target; when `editor.tutorialRunner` is nil (exit) both hide. Observers (block-based, `[weak self]`, registered once in `observe()`): the runner notification; the served window's `willClose` (sets `editor.tutorialRunner = nil`, hides both — closing the window or the project ends the tutorial), `didMove`/`didResize` (re-place the panel), `didMiniaturize`/`didDeminiaturize` (hide/show both). The coach holds editor and runner only weakly and has no `deinit` work.
4. **The panel (TU-4, TU-10).** `TutorialPanel`: `[.titled, .nonactivatingPanel, .utilityWindow]`, title "Tutorial", no close box, `level = .floating`, `hidesOnDeactivate = false`, `becomesKeyOnlyIfNeeded = true`, `canBecomeKey`/`canBecomeMain` false, no editable or selectable text. Card 320 pt wide from `DS` tokens and `Controls.swift`'s `StickerButton` (Show Me and Next `.primary`, the rest `.secondary`), square chrome. Rows: title (`tutorial.title`), progress `Step n of m` (`tutorial.progress`) with the tick (`tutorial.tick`, SF Symbol `checkmark.circle.fill`, `DS.accent`), the sentence (`tutorial.text`, wrapping, `TutorialSentence.attributed`: `DS.sans(13)`, bold `DS.sans(13, weight: .semibold)`, code `DS.mono(12)`), the message (`tutorial.message`, wrapping, `DS.textMuted`, hidden when nil), buttons `tutorial.<raw>` titled Back, Show Me, Skip, Next, Exit, Open Practice Project, Close. **Step mode** shows exactly the runner's `offers` in its order; all but Exit disabled while `showMeRunning`. **Finished**: progress `Finished`, text `You finished this tutorial.`, buttons Back, Exit (titled Done). **Message**, first that holds: the last Show Me's error when its step is the current step; `Show Me exports to <path abbreviated with ~>.` when `lastShowMe.paths` is non-empty; `revealRefused`. **Tick**: a change whose `lastCompleted` is a new `(step, .wait)` shows that step's number and sentence with the tick and every button disabled for `tickHold`, then renders the runner (`Timer`, main, `[weak self]`). Placement: `panelOrigin` — right of the editor 12 pt, tops aligned, when it fits the screen's `visibleFrame`; else left of it; else inside the editor's bottom-left corner, 16 pt in; re-placed on move/resize; `fitWindowToContent` keeps its top-left (the recorder's rule).
5. **Resolver (TU-11).** `kind(of:)`: `inspector.tab.<t>` → tab, `inspector.sub_tab.<s>` → sub-tab, other fixed names → `.view(name)`, `section:<id>` (id in `TutorialTargets.sections`) → section, `clip:$selection|$created` → clip. `resolve`: `.view` → the first non-hidden view under the editor window's content view, or under its attached sheet's content view for `sheet.export.*`, whose accessibility id equals the name; tab → the `PanelTabsView` among the inspector's descendants, `InspectorTabBadge.tabRect(index:)`; sub-tab → the `ClipSubTabsView`, `cellRect(tabs.firstIndex(of:))`; section → `inspector.shownPane()?.1.sections` by id; clip → the earliest clip of the current selection (`$selection`) or the runner's `created`, `TimelineLayout.clipRect` on `timeline.content`. Every rect is intersected with that view's `visibleRect` and converted to its window's content view. **Never the wrong place:** a view hidden, not in the window, or with an empty visible intersection answers `rect` nil and a one-sentence `reason` (`<the table's description, capitalised> is not on screen now.`; `The export sheet is not open.`; `The Clip tab does not show the <Title> sub-tab now.`; `The inspector does not show the <id> section now.`; `No clip is selected.`). `bringIntoView`: a clip target → `TimelineView.reveal(_:)`; anything else nothing (the runner's reveal already scrolled the section).
6. **Spotlight (TU-4, TU-11).** `TutorialSpotlightWindow`: borderless, `ignoresMouseEvents`, clear, not opaque, no shadow, `canBecomeKey` false; a child (`addChildWindow(_:ordered: .above)`) of the window that holds the target — the editor's, or its attached sheet for `sheet.export.*` — re-parented when that changes; its frame is that window's content view frame in screen coordinates; one `TutorialRingView` (`hitTest` nil, 2 pt `DS.accent` square stroke inside its bounds) at the spot's rect outset by 4. No target, a nil rect, a finished tutorial → ring hidden (window ordered out). `show` with `stepChanged` calls `bringIntoView` once, then resolves. **Follows layout** by `refreshSoon()` — one coalesced `DispatchQueue.main.async` (a documented seam) — from: `NSView.frameDidChangeNotification` and `boundsDidChangeNotification` with object nil, kept only when the view's window is the editor's or its sheet (never the spotlight's own); the editor window's `didResize`, `willBeginSheet`, `didEndSheet`; `projectDocumentDidChange` of the served document; the runner notification. Observers live only while a target is shown.
7. **Dev tools and `snapshot_ui`.** `UISnapshot.openWindow(.tutorial)` finds the visible window whose controller is `TutorialPanelController`; `kind(of:)` answers `tutorial` for it and `spotlight` for a `TutorialSpotlightWindow` (before the `NSPanel` arm). Staging: for `window: editor` with no `view`, and for `window: sheet`, when `TutorialCoach.shared.spotlight.ringFrame(in: subject.window)` is non-nil, a fresh `TutorialRingView` at that frame is added as the root's last subview (never skipped by the layout dump) and removed in `unstage` — so the capture shows the ring and the dump holds `tutorial.spotlight`'s frame. `tutorial_press` reaches the coach's panel only on main, polls Show Me with `AgentLane.releasingLock` as `tutorial_step` does.
8. **Checker.** `tutorial_probe.swift` answers `unresolvable`: every fixed name, `section:<id>` for every table section and both clip refs, for which `TutorialTargetResolver.kind(of:)` is nil. `tutorial_check.py` fails on a non-empty or missing list; selftest `target-unresolvable` sets `["timeline.clips"]`.
9. **Proof `tutorial_chrome_proof.py [--only ID,…]`.** It launches `proof_app.binary()` itself (`graphic_browser_proof.py`'s way) in a scratch home `work/tutorial_chrome/home` (with `Movies/` made) with `-RCDevAppearance light` for every row, then `dark` for S rows; stops each by pid; `close_project {discard: true}` (after `cancel_sheet` when a sheet is up) ends each row, a refused close failing it. `plain()` is re-implemented in Python. Rows: **T1** log clean. **H1** `perform_menu_item` listing: under Help ▸ Tutorials, the guide's page titles in file order each holding its tutorials' `displayTitle`s, then Open Practice Project last. **K1** on `new_project {practice: true}`, Dawn selected, `select_inspector_tab {tab: clip, sub_tab: sound}`: `tutorial_state {target}` for every non-sheet fixed name, every section of the Sound pane, `clip:$selection`; then File ▸ Export… and the nine `sheet.export.*`: each view target's rect equals (±0.5) its id's dump frame (`snapshot_ui window editor|sheet`, `fill_preview false`) intersected with every ancestor `NSClipView` frame, or is nil with a reason exactly when that is empty; tabs and Dawn's offered sub-tabs equal the strip arithmetic; un-offered sub-tabs nil with a reason; at least one Sound section clipped or hidden (precondition, printed). **M-<id>** each of the five started by `perform_menu_item ["Help","Tutorials",<page title>,<displayTitle>]` on the practice project (its `windows_opened` holds a `tutorial` row), then per step: `panel` mode step, progress `Step k of n`, text == plain(runner text), buttons == the offers mapped in order; `ring.target` == the step's spotlight, and when shown its rect equals the dump's target frame (clipped) and the editor/sheet capture's staged `tutorial.spotlight` frame is that rect outset by 4; then `tutorial_press` show_me, else next, else skip, waiting ≤3 s for the panel to show the runner's step. Export a range: steps 4–5 `ring.window` `sheet`; finished panel message `Show Me exports to ~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4.` (the scratch home's), the export waited for. ## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

95	    /// The table as JSON-ready values, for the checker:

97	    /// "clip_refs", "tabs", "sub_tabs"}`, a tab by its title lowercased and a
98	    /// sub-tab by its raw value — the spellings a step's `reveal` uses.
99	    static func manifest() -> [String: Any] {
100	        var homes: [String: Any] = [:]
101	        for (id, home) in sections {
102	            homes[id] = [
103	                "tab": home.tab.title.lowercased(),
104	                "sub_tab": home.subTab.map { $0.rawValue as Any } ?? NSNull(),
105	            ] as [String: Any]
106	        }
107	        return [
108	            "fixed": fixed.keys.sorted(),
109	            "sections": homes,
110	            "clip_refs": clipRefs,
111	            "tabs": InspectorTab.allCases.map { $0.title.lowercased() },
112	            "sub_tabs": ClipSubTab.allCases.map(\.rawValue),
113	        ]
114	    }
115	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  pages (spec §11 W-15): `CaptionLooks` (`slide`, `fill`, `dim`; `.none`;

  and `CaptionStyle.wordStyle(_:)`, the preset with the live looks turned

  `isFiller`, and `MediaTranscript.captionWords(for:in:)`, `words(for:in:)`

  transcript when its marker serves `.captions` (`cloudWords`); otherwise the

  network. The handler's first line reads

  the assistant's Stop ends the run (amends AI-16). An optional `from`/`to`

  `overlapping`, both engines alike), and the on-device run hears only the
  window plus `recognitionPadSeconds` each side (`recognitionJob`).

  language in the package's `cache/device-transcripts/`, keyed by the
  file's source stamp, the language, the OS version and `version`, each run
  a heard source span and its words in source ticks. `heard(...)` answers
  from a stored run that contains the call's span, else recognises and
  stores (dropping runs the new one contains), never after a cancel or a
  file change during the run; written through `CacheLedger`. Captions,
  the filler tools and the cloud readers never read it.
- `CaptionPages.swift` — word-caption PAGES (spec §11 W-7), pure and
  synchronous so it runs on whichever engine thread calls it:
  `normalize` (trim, split, sort, the per-engine `lead` — its ONE home —
  and the clamp into the job's `span`, a word pushed off the end on the
  clip's last frame), the pager (speaker, 0.25 s gap, sentence mark,
  3 s, `maxWords`, and the MEASURED width through
  `LayerRenderers.measuredSize`), the balance step once per width
  break, the clause preference, shrink-then-wrap for a lone word, and
  page timing that abuts under `breakGap` and never passes the span.
  `cues(...)` is what both engines call: `.subtitles` goes to
  `CaptionCues.build`, untouched. `samplePage` is `cues(...)`'s first page
  over a span past the words' hold — the sheet's preview page, a real one,
  balance step included. Pauses are word gaps and punctuation;
  `SilenceDetector`/`MediaSpeech` are not consulted.
- `CaptionImporter.swift` (SubRip grammar) · `CaptionExporter.swift` (`.srt` /
  `.vtt` from one all-text track, never guessed; a popup built from
  `NSMenuItem`s carrying `representedObject`, because `addItem(withTitle:)`
  REMOVES a same-titled row).

  serial queue and the main-thread completion; `transcribe` is the
  synchronous body — the janitor FIRST, the jobs grouped by MEDIA, each

  `transcriptWritten` and `stampWritten`, `cached`,
  `janitorDeleted`, `janitorFailed`, `janitorDeferred`, `held`, and
  `refusedUndeleted` — a transcript refused after it was made whose DELETE
  failed, owed to the dashboard with no retry, R6-20) and owns the
  shared cleanup warning wording for the sheet and MCP result or failure.
  `billedSeconds` is the ONE sum of `audioSeconds` — each term floored at 0,
  saturating at `Int.max` — that the bill sentence and `audio_seconds` read;
  `cacheWarnings` is one sentence per uploaded media whose marker did not
  land, and promises nothing about the next run.
  A nil client admits only a nonempty, entirely
  current batch and skips janitor/network, retaining pending IDs as deferred.
  One media's failure is one media's problem (the catch first records a
  `Refusal` whose DELETE `failed` in `refusedUndeleted`, then reads its
  `ClientError`) and the run carries on, with exactly two exceptions: a CANCEL
  and a REFUSED KEY. `+Media` holds `retryDeletes` and `fetch` — the ten-hour

  every exit, the server's model and language filtered through
  `withoutCredential` and then bounded at 64 Unicode scalars (`bounded`,

  whose served strings — every key and value at any depth, scanned from the
  bytes (`TranscriptWord.servedStrings`, R6-23) — repeat the key refused

  written before its marker, and the DELETE last with its answer recorded —
  its `remote_deleted` rewrite only over a first write that landed (#187).

  `janitorFailed` is never fetched, since its cache file is the one record of
  the id still owed a delete.

  `money`, over `AssemblyAIRates`' two dated constants. Spec §11's R6-13: a

  cost if the delete clears. `facts(jobs:media:cacheDirectory:)` is the ONE

  keystroke. `canReuseWithoutCredential` is true only for nonempty all-cached
  rows and gates the keyless sheet. Its classification is deliberately NOT shared with
  `CloudTranscriber`'s — one says what a run WOULD do, the other what it DID
  — and a probe row compares them.
- `CloudProgress.swift` — the cloud run's one number and the words beside it,

  four phases at 0.25 / 0.65 / 0.95, the submit holding at the upload's end

  147× and holding, and the five detail lines, a count under a megabyte spelt
  `<1`. The run publishes
  `max(previous, computed)`.
- `AssemblyAITranscript.swift` — the wire VALUES, and
  `TranscriptOptions.keyterms`, the ONE spelling of the vocabulary's
  trim/de-duplicate/cap that the sheet's field and the tool's argument share:
  `TranscriptOptions`,
  `TranscriptRequest` (whose `encode` is the whole wire body — `language_code`
  absent for auto, `keyterms_prompt` absent when empty), `TranscriptWord`

  `.fillers` also needs the marker's own `disfluencies` true.

  with nil as `null`** through

  that carries the key is never sent or accepted. `delete` answers THREE
  states (`deleted`, `failed`, `notSent`): an id that is not sendable is never
  put on the wire. `delete(id:cancel:)` reads the run's token as a STOP and
  never attaches it: a DELETE is cut `deleteAfterStop` (2 s) of wall clock
  after the later of the Stop and its own start and answers `failed`, owed
  like any other (R6-19); `send`'s `stop`/`grace` and `+Session`'s
  `waitForReply` are that bound. `+Session` also holds `ClientError`'s two
  readings, `isRetriable` and `shortName`, moved out at the cap. `+Submission`
  owns the single paid submit and R6-14's
  bounded recovery: three newest-page looks for an exact uploaded URL, with
  no retry of the POST or requests by any unrelated id.
- `AssemblyAIConfiguration.swift` · `AssemblyAILanguages.swift` ·
  `SecretStore.swift` — WHERE the client speaks and WHAT it says it is.
  `AssemblyAIConfiguration` is the ONE reader of `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` and
  `-RCSecretFolder`, both out of the ARGUMENT domain only (its `argument` is
  the one argument-domain reader, which `AssistantConfiguration` and
  `DevAssistantLaunch` reuse), and the ONE line
  in the feature that names `AppSupport.directory` (spec §11's R6-9: with an
  endpoint set and no secret folder, `store()` answers an EMPTY `MemoryStore`
  so a proof never opens the person's key). `FileStore` has a `name`:
  `assemblyai-key` by default, `anthropic-key` for the assistant's key
  (AI-8, AI-13, whose `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` plays R6-9's endpoint). Non-`https` is accepted only for
  `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `::1`. `FileStore` creates its file with
  `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` at `0600` under a temporary name and `rename(2)`s it, in a
  directory `AppSupport.ensureDirectory` makes, `0700` at each level it makes
  — never `chmod`ed after; `MemoryStore` is
  the probe's. The language table is a DATED static list, not an authority:
  a code AssemblyAI refuses comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence.
- `MediaTranscript.swift` — `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` and its
  `.complete.json` sidecar (`MediaImporter.transcriptsKind` is the post kind,
  and lives beside the other three in `MediaCacheFiles.swift`). The provider's
  `words` are stored VERBATIM as BYTES: `File.encoded()` splices `wordsJSON`
  in after a `.sortedKeys` header, `init(data:)` cuts it back out with
  `JSONValueRange`, and neither ever re-serialises — a `0.98` does not
  survive that. Both `File` inits throw on a `words` that is not an array, so
  `read` answers nil and `isCurrent` false rather than caching zero words;
  `isCurrent` asks `serves(_:for: .captions)`.
  THE MAPPING is here: a word is a clip's when `in ≤ start × 600 <
  in + duration × speed`, landing at `start + (m − in) / speed`, clamped
  through `Transcriber.placed` (R6-10). That `× 600` goes through
  `sourceTicks(milliseconds:)`, the one integer multiply on the caption
  path, clamped in `Int` to ±`Ticks.max / 600` first and deliberately NOT to
  `maxSourceTicks` (R6-10's extension). A RAMPED clip's job carries
  `Transcriber.Job.ramp` and lands a word at `clip.start + S⁻¹(m)` through
  its `SourceMap`, its window `[in, in + S(D))` (SR-20 (d)); the
  three-argument `Transcriber.jobs(for:in:urls:)` stays for the instruments
  and refuses a ramped clip.
  `undeleted(in:)` is the janitor's.
- `SpeechEngine.swift` — the on-device engine (`SpeechAnalyzer`,
  `SpeechTranscriber`, `AssetInventory`) and the ONE file under
  `app/Sources` that imports Speech or says `async` for it (spec §11 W-8).
  Every entry point is synchronous or a main-queue completion: `transcribe`
  refuses main by precondition and blocks its caller on a semaphore a
  `Task.detached` analysis signals, waited for in 0.1 s slices so a cancel
  answers at once, bounded at max(120, 4× the audio); the asks
  (`supportedLocales`, `installedLocales`, `isInstalled`) answer `[]` or nil
  past `askBound` (10 s); `download` is the Download row's alone and no tool
  calls it. **Never `Task {}` here** — a main-thread caller's actor would be
  inherited and the semaphore would deadlock. `Handle` is what
  `CancelToken` holds for a running analysis. Two host facts it is built on
  (road map 8 §10.6): `status(forModules:)` is `.installed` only for a
  RESERVED locale, so `isInstalled` reserves, reads and releases what it
  reserved; and `release(reservedLocale:)` matches the framework's own
  spelling (`fr_FR`, not `fr-FR`), so a release walks `reservedLocales` by
  BCP-47 tag. Every path that constructs a transcriber releases on every
  exit (a cap of 5). Reserve → status → release and every release run one
  at a time, in arrival order, through the `Gate` actor; `releaseNow` is the
  in-gate form, and an analysis or a download SIGNALS its caller before it
  queues its release, so a stalled gate cannot hold a finished run hostage.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is

long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`

  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in

  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,

  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s

  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is

  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).

  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  `CaptionCues.build`, untouched. `samplePage` is `cues(...)`'s first page

  land, and promises nothing about the next run.

  and a REFUSED KEY. `+Media` holds `retryDeletes` and `fetch` — the ten-hour

  every exit, the server's model and language filtered through
  `withoutCredential` and then bounded at 64 Unicode scalars (`bounded`,

  cost if the delete clears. `facts(jobs:media:cacheDirectory:)` is the ONE

  keystroke. `canReuseWithoutCredential` is true only for nonempty all-cached
  rows and gates the keyless sheet. Its classification is deliberately NOT shared with

  — and a probe row compares them.

  PURE: a share per media TO UPLOAD (cached and held media have none), the
  four phases at 0.25 / 0.65 / 0.95, the submit holding at the upload's end
  (0.65) with a line of its own, the wait advancing on the clock against q8's
  147× and holding, and the five detail lines, a count under a megabyte spelt
  `<1`. The run publishes
  `max(previous, computed)`.

  `TranscriptOptions.keyterms`, the ONE spelling of the vocabulary's
  trim/de-duplicate/cap that the sheet's field and the tool's argument share:
  `TranscriptOptions`,
  `TranscriptRequest` (whose `encode` is the whole wire body — `language_code`
  absent for auto, `keyterms_prompt` absent when empty), `TranscriptWord`

  `TranscriptResponse` and `JSONValueRange`. `TranscriptStamp.swift` owns the
  cache marker: `TranscriptSourceStamp` projects `CacheStamp` to size,
  modification second, duration and audio presence, then pairs those with

  `.fillers` also needs the marker's own `disfluencies` true.

  its marker have to carry; `TranscriptResponse` reads `words` through a
  `try?` so the CLIENT's rule about a missing words array is the sentence a
  caller gets.

  answers nil, so a 3xx is `.redirected` and the credential reaches no other
  host; an upload retries once on a 5xx or a transport error and never on a
  4xx or after a cancel; `poll` sleeps in ≤ 0.1 s slices that read the token

  the polled id is `.malformed` too (`requireEchoedID` in `+Session`, #71), so
  the id `fetch` stores and deletes is always the submitted one. `note` writes
  straight to fd 1 through `FileHandle.standardOutput`, never `print`, so a
  file-redirected log is complete (#116). `request` and `send` stay in the
  first file, with `withoutCredential(_:)` beside them: those three are the
  members that touch `credential`, and that helper keeps the three sentences
  the client RELAYS verbatim — a 402's, a 4xx's and a transcript's `error` —
  from carrying a key a server echoed back; `relayed` (`+Session`) then cuts
  each to 300 Unicode scalars (R6-23). `isSendableIdentifier`
  (`+Session`: `isPlainIdentifier` AND not `carriesCredential`) is the ONE id
  gate — `poll`, `delete`, a submit reply and a recovery-list row — so an id
  that carries the key is never sent or accepted. `delete` answers THREE
  states (`deleted`, `failed`, `notSent`): an id that is not sendable is never
  put on the wire. `delete(id:cancel:)` reads the run's token as a STOP and
  never attaches it: a DELETE is cut `deleteAfterStop` (2 s) of wall clock
  after the later of the Stop and its own start and answers `failed`, owed
  like any other (R6-19); `send`'s `stop`/`grace` and `+Session`'s
  `waitForReply` are that bound. `+Session` also holds `ClientError`'s two
  readings, `isRetriable` and `shortName`, moved out at the cap. `+Submission`
  owns the single paid submit and R6-14's
  bounded recovery: three newest-page looks for an exact uploaded URL, with
  no retry of the POST or requests by any unrelated id.
- `AssemblyAIConfiguration.swift` · `AssemblyAILanguages.swift` ·
  `SecretStore.swift` — WHERE the client speaks and WHAT it says it is.
  `AssemblyAIConfiguration` is the ONE reader of `-RCAssemblyAIEndpoint` and
  `-RCSecretFolder`, both out of the ARGUMENT domain only (its `argument` is
  the one argument-domain reader, which `AssistantConfiguration` and
  `DevAssistantLaunch` reuse), and the ONE line
  in the feature that names `AppSupport.directory` (spec §11's R6-9: with an
  endpoint set and no secret folder, `store()` answers an EMPTY `MemoryStore`
  so a proof never opens the person's key). `FileStore` has a `name`:
  `assemblyai-key` by default, `anthropic-key` for the assistant's key
  (AI-8, AI-13, whose `RC_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` plays R6-9's endpoint). Non-`https` is accepted only for
  `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `::1`. `FileStore` creates its file with
  `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` at `0600` under a temporary name and `rename(2)`s it, in a
  directory `AppSupport.ensureDirectory` makes, `0700` at each level it makes
  — never `chmod`ed after; `MemoryStore` is
  the probe's. The language table is a DATED static list, not an authority:
  a code AssemblyAI refuses comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence.
- `MediaTranscript.swift` — `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` and its
  `.complete.json` sidecar (`MediaImporter.transcriptsKind` is the post kind,
  and lives beside the other three in `MediaCacheFiles.swift`). The provider's
  `words` are stored VERBATIM as BYTES: `File.encoded()` splices `wordsJSON`
  in after a `.sortedKeys` header, `init(data:)` cuts it back out with
  `JSONValueRange`, and neither ever re-serialises — a `0.98` does not
  survive that. Both `File` inits throw on a `words` that is not an array, so
  `read` answers nil and `isCurrent` false rather than caching zero words;
  `isCurrent` asks `serves(_:for: .captions)`.
  THE MAPPING is here: a word is a clip's when `in ≤ start × 600 <
  in + duration × speed`, landing at `start + (m − in) / speed`, clamped
  through `Transcriber.placed` (R6-10). That `× 600` goes through
  `sourceTicks(milliseconds:)`, the one integer multiply on the caption
  path, clamped in `Int` to ±`Ticks.max / 600` first and deliberately NOT to

  and refuses a ramped clip.

- `SpeechEngine.swift` — the on-device engine (`SpeechAnalyzer`,
  `SpeechTranscriber`, `AssetInventory`) and the ONE file under
  `app/Sources` that imports Speech or says `async` for it (spec §11 W-8).

  calls it. **Never `Task {}` here** — a main-thread caller's actor would be
  inherited and the semaphore would deadlock. `Handle` is what
  `CancelToken` holds for a running analysis. Two host facts it is built on

  RESERVED locale, so `isInstalled` reserves, reads and releases what it

  spelling (`fr_FR`, not `fr-FR`), so a release walks `reservedLocales` by

  exit (a cap of 5). Reserve → status → release and every release run one
  at a time, in arrival order, through the `Gate` actor; `releaseNow` is the
  in-gate form, and an analysis or a download SIGNALS its caller before it

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,

  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is

  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an

  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- Pitfalls, each measured: **a section factory is not a section until
  `makeSections()` calls it** — nothing type-checks the omission, and two
  phases shipped a section invisible in the app; `editedList` — a write of a
  list-valued key is built from the list it is about to REPLACE (the action's
  end list, else the base), never the evaluated one; the collapsed-state
  `UserDefaults` key records COLLAPSED, so `defaultExpanded` applies only when
  nothing is stored; a field's `refresh` is skipped while its field editor is
  attached, which it still is inside `controlTextDidEndEditing`; the pane's
  low-priority bottom pin is **249**, one below `.defaultLow`, because at 250
  it tied with a section's hugging and the solver picked per PROCESS; and
  `rebuild()` destroys every control and preserves no first responder, so a

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  inherited and the semaphore would deadlock. `Handle` is what

117	            })
118	    }

3	/// The Assistant tab's question dot (spec §11 AI-19): a small accent-coloured
4	/// dot just right of "Assistant" in the inspector's tab strip, shown while
5	/// the window's assistant waits on an ask-first question, whichever tab is
6	/// showing.
7	///
8	/// Its own view laid over the strip rather than a fork of `PanelTabsView`
9	/// (`Controls.swift` is carried from Rasterize and kept in sync), so it
10	/// mirrors `PanelTabsView.tabRect`'s arithmetic and the way the strip centres
11	/// a title, as `ClipSubTabsView.cellRect` does. It is the inspector root's
12	/// LAST subview, above the container `buildTabs()` refills on every tab
13	/// change. Passive: it takes no click (`hitTest` answers nil, so a click
14	/// reaches the strip) and no key.
15	final class InspectorTabBadge: NSView {
16	    static let identifier = "inspector.assistant.badge"
17	    static let diameter: CGFloat = 6
18	    static let gap: CGFloat = 3
19	
20	    init() {
21	        super.init(frame: .zero)
22	        isHidden = true
23	        translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
24	        setAccessibilityIdentifier(Self.identifier)
25	    }
26	
27	    @available(*, unavailable)
28	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
29	        fatalError("InspectorTabBadge does not support NSCoder")
30	    }
31	
32	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
33	
34	    override func hitTest(_ point: NSPoint) -> NSView? { nil }
35	
36	    override func setFrameSize(_ newSize: NSSize) {
37	        super.setFrameSize(newSize)
38	        needsDisplay = true
39	    }
40	
41	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
42	        DS.accent.setFill()
43	        NSBezierPath(
44	            ovalIn: Self.dotRect(stripWidth: bounds.width, stripHeight: bounds.height)
45	        ).fill()
46	    }
47	
48	    /// Added to `root` with its four edges on `strip`'s.
49	    func install(over strip: NSView, in root: NSView) {
50	        root.addSubview(self)
51	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
52	            topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: strip.topAnchor),
53	            bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: strip.bottomAnchor),
54	            leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: strip.leadingAnchor),
55	            trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: strip.trailingAnchor),
56	        ])
57	    }
58	
59	    /// `PanelTabsView.tabRect`'s arithmetic (equal widths, `.rounded()`
60	    /// edges) for the Assistant tab of `InspectorTab.allCases.count`.
61	    static func tabRect(stripWidth: CGFloat, stripHeight: CGFloat) -> NSRect {
62	        let index = InspectorTab.assistant.rawValue
63	        let width = stripWidth / CGFloat(max(InspectorTab.allCases.count, 1))
64	        let left = (CGFloat(index) * width).rounded()
65	        let right = (CGFloat(index + 1) * width).rounded()
66	        return NSRect(x: left, y: 0, width: right - left, height: stripHeight)
67	    }
68	
69	    /// The Assistant title in the active tab's font, centred in `tabRect`
70	    /// exactly as `PanelTabsView` draws a title. The semibold face is the
71	    /// wider of the strip's two, so the dot clears the word either way.
72	    static func titleRect(stripWidth: CGFloat, stripHeight: CGFloat) -> NSRect {
73	        let tab = tabRect(stripWidth: stripWidth, stripHeight: stripHeight)
74	        let size = InspectorTab.assistant.title.size(
75	            withAttributes: [.font: DS.sans(12, weight: .semibold)])
76	        return NSRect(
77	            x: tab.midX - size.width / 2, y: tab.midY - size.height / 2,
78	            width: size.width, height: size.height)
79	    }
80	
81	    /// Just right of the title, never past the tab's trailing edge less 2 pt.
82	    static func dotRect(stripWidth: CGFloat, stripHeight: CGFloat) -> NSRect {
83	        let tab = tabRect(stripWidth: stripWidth, stripHeight: stripHeight)
84	        let title = titleRect(stripWidth: stripWidth, stripHeight: stripHeight)
85	        let x = min(title.maxX + gap, tab.maxX - 2 - diameter).rounded()
86	        let y = (tab.midY - diameter / 2).rounded()
87	        return NSRect(x: x, y: y, width: diameter, height: diameter)
88	    }
89	}
